artworks.title: Cassiopeia
artworks.description: Cameron's albumen print (Metropolitan Museum of Art) stages the Ethiopian queen as a Victorian allegory — Cassiopeia's boast against the Nereids distilled into a single seated figure whose vanity still names a northern constellation.

artworks.title: Perseus and Andromeda
artworks.description: Matham's engraving after Goltzius returns to the crisis Cassiopeia caused: Andromeda chained for the sea-monster while the royal parents' boast still hangs over the shore — the queen's vanity as the hinge of the Ethiopian rescue.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Harryhausen's epic keeps Cassiopeia's courtly vanity as the spark that dooms Andromeda to the rock — the queen whose comparison with the goddesses buys a daughter's sacrifice.

popCulture.title: Cassiopeia (constellation)
popCulture.description: The boastful queen was set among the stars as the W-shaped northern constellation — punished to circle the pole, still the most recognizable mythic signature in the autumn sky.

popCulture.title: Cassiopeia (mother of Andromeda)
popCulture.description: Wife of Cepheus and mother of Andromeda — the Ethiopian queen whose vanity against the Nereids remains the cautionary opening of every Perseus rescue.
